# Independent discovery — volunteer oral-history deposits

**Stage:** investigator, A5-01-control. **Pre-release discovery:** the exact plan has not been sought or read. This file is intended to be frozen by the required reveal helper; do not edit it after that hash is recorded.

## Scope and initial direction

The society receives a mix of volunteer WAVs, photographs and notes, wants stable identity and metadata, keeps received audio apart from access copies, and cannot standardize recording applications. The safest pilot starts with an immutable-as-received copy and a package-level identity/relationship record; optional metadata enrichment and access derivatives happen later on identified copies. This is a planning recommendation, not a product capability claim.

Use an interview/event ID and distinct file IDs for each received recording, photo, note, transcript revision and access derivative. Keep the submitted filename and donor/device metadata as received alongside any staff-normalized description. Record the link from each file to its interview, and from each transcript revision or derivative to its source object. Have the collections archivist decide which descriptive fields are authoritative and how conflicting donor, interviewer, recorder and staff statements are retained. This avoids relying on filenames, recorder-specific tags or transcript text as a unique key.

## Two deposit workflows and a preservation analogue

1. **Package-first, sidecar-authoritative (recommended pilot baseline).** Retain originals untouched in a BagIt-style transfer directory, with the audio, photographs, notes, optional plain-text transcript and access files under `data/`; place an UTF-8 CSV/JSON descriptive record and a compact relationship/revision log with the package. Use stable IDs and relative paths. BagIt 1.0 treats payload files as opaque byte streams and its payload manifest lists every payload path with a checksum. This is recorder- and format-agnostic and can include mixed media, but the society must keep sidecars and relative paths together and define their schema. A manifest detects changes from the time it is made; it does not itself establish descriptive authority, transcript approval, ongoing redundant storage or consent. [S06, S12]

2. **BWF-aware enrichment (optional after intake).** A staff member can use BWF MetaEdit on a working copy of a compatible WAVE file to add a deliberately small, approved BWF metadata subset, validate it and export a report; the sidecar record remains authoritative for full descriptions, complex identifiers and transcript/version relationships. BWF metadata travels with WAVE files in BWF-aware applications, while ordinary WAV playback can still work in software that does not expose the BWF metadata. The tradeoff is field/encoding/tool variation and the need to write a new file. Preserve the received source separately, keep a package-level whole-file manifest, compare the tool's audio-data-only digest, and independently check output fields and playback before accepting a derivative. [S01–S04]

**Preservation analogue:** BagIt gives a simple, portable transfer/fixity envelope for arbitrary files; PREMIS 3.0 offers a more formal model for object identifiers, derivation/structural relationships, dated events, agents and outcomes. A small pilot can borrow the pattern without adopting full PREMIS: log ingest/fixity, transcript correction approval, derivative creation, tool/version, date, operator and outcome. Neither a bag nor a metadata standard alone guarantees preservation; storage copies, access policy and periodic fixity are still owner/system responsibilities. [S06–S07]

## Evidence-led findings and conditions

- BWF has a required `bext` chunk, but not every descriptive field is mandatory. FADGI 2021 labels `Originator`, `OriginatorReference` and `Description` strongly recommended; `OriginatorReference` is limited to 32 characters and `Description` to 256; `OriginationDate` is 10 characters. FADGI's `OriginationDate` application describes a file-creation date in the archive's local time zone, so do not silently treat it as the interview-event date. Some INFO fields are recommended or optional. An empty/unsupported field should stay empty rather than receive guessed data. [S01–S02]
- WAVE is a wrapper whose audio fidelity depends on the codec; `.wav` alone does not prove PCM, BWF conformance or lossless behavior. BWF MetaEdit can export/validate metadata and compute an MD5 of the WAVE `data` chunk (audio bitstream only), while a BagIt manifest can track the whole file. Use distinct checks for bitstream preservation and file-level fixity. Do not promise lossless edit behavior based on extension. [S02–S03, S13]
- Encoding is a material round-trip risk. A BWF MetaEdit issue reported Windows-1252-style curly quotation characters not translating correctly (issue #29, 2017). Release history lists ASCII-support work in 20.05/20.08, then 23.04 support for CP437/850/858, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1/-2 plus CSET read/write. The FADGI guide says CSET/code page determines text encoding for internal metadata and absent/zero defaults to ISO-8859/1. This is evidence of evolving support, not proof that every recorder/editor/player round-trips Unicode or other code pages. Keep UTF-8 sidecars authoritative; test representative names, punctuation and languages on the exact toolchain before optional embedding. [S01, S04–S05]
- The Library of Congress Veterans History Project treats transcript and recording as complementary and asks transcript creators to identify transcriber/editor/date and mark when/how a transcript differs from the recording. The project says transcripts are welcome but not required. The W3C WAI guidance calls for transcripts and accessible players. For this brief, keep the plain-text transcript and listening copy as explicitly optional, human-reviewed access companions; do not make either replace the original or block deposit when unavailable. Preserve transcript revisions separately or version them, and require interviewer approval for corrections as the brief directs. [S08–S09]
- OHMS (University of Kentucky Nunn Center) is a useful unfamiliar access option: it links searchable transcript/index text to moments in online oral-history audio/video. The official project offers a free account, while the public viewer is software that must be hosted/customized and tested with media links. Treat it as a later access-layer candidate, not a deposit format or preservation store; evaluate hosting, media accessibility, consent and staff capacity first. A pilot can retain ordinary text and audio independent of OHMS. [S10–S11]

## Owners, boundaries and unresolved inputs

The collections archivist owns descriptive-field authority. The interviewer approves transcript corrections. Consent review is an external owner input; neither possession nor a software default grants consent. Model consent/access states explicitly, with an unreviewed/restricted state until the owner decision is supplied, but do not invent the review authority or policy. No automatic speech recognition is required. Do not alter received originals during research; never infer losslessness from a filename extension; keep access derivatives distinct and record their process and source.

Unresolved for the owners: the controlled identifier format; the field authority/order and conflict policy; whether optional embedded fields and transcript/listening derivative are wanted; which consent evidence and access actions are approved; whether the society can host a web access layer; and the target audience/player and accessibility acceptance criteria. Publicly answerable questions about BWF fields, BagIt fixity, encoding caveats and transcript/access patterns have been investigated and should not be deferred to those decisions.

## Checks status

No local files were modified as research inputs; no audio, transcript or metadata round-trip was executed, and no executable media tool was run. Sources below are research evidence only, not validation of a proposed product or workflow. Proposed checks belong in the post-release draft: verify IDs and links; verify complete BagIt manifest and checksum on receipt; confirm originals remain byte-identical; test BWF field lengths/defaults and encoding across at least two readers; compare data-chunk digest before/after any metadata edit; identify codec from the file structure and sample-play derivatives; have a reviewer confirm transcript revision provenance and accessibility using the intended player. Mark each NOT_RUN unless actually performed.
